questions.q: GDPR applies to the personal data of people in the EU based on which factor?
options: Where the person whose data it is is located, regardless of where the processing organization is based
Only where the processing organization has a registered EU office
Only to data stored on servers physically located in the EU
Only to companies with more than 500 EU employees
questions.explain: GDPR has extraterritorial scope: it protects EU residents' personal data no matter where the organization processing it is headquartered.

questions.q: What is the clearest distinction between GDPR's and CCPA's consent models, as covered in this lesson?
options: GDPR is opt-in (processing needs permission first); CCPA is opt-out (collection is allowed by default until the consumer opts out)
GDPR and CCPA use the exact same opt-in model
CCPA is opt-in and GDPR is opt-out
Neither law addresses consent at all
questions.explain: GDPR requires an affirmative legal basis before processing (opt-in); CCPA permits collection/sale by default unless the consumer actively opts out — opposite defaults toward the same goal of consumer control.

questions.q: Under GDPR, what is the maximum fine described in this lesson for serious violations?
options: Up to €20 million or 4% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher
A flat €1,000 per affected individual
There is no monetary penalty, only a warning letter
Loss of the company's EU business license only
questions.explain: GDPR Article 83 sets fines up to €20 million or 4% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher, for the most serious violations.

questions.q: Who does HIPAA's Privacy Rule directly bind, per this lesson?
options: Covered entities (health plans, clearinghouses, providers who transmit health information electronically) and their business associates
Every company in the United States, regardless of industry
Only hospitals, and no other type of healthcare organization
Only software vendors that build electronic health record systems
questions.explain: HIPAA's Privacy Rule governs covered entities — health plans, healthcare clearinghouses, and providers who transmit health information electronically — plus their business associates.

questions.q: Which right is explicitly listed in this lesson as one GDPR grants to individuals (data subjects)?
options: Erasure, also known as the 'right to be forgotten'
The right to a free annual credit report
The right to sue for breach of contract in any jurisdiction
The right to unlimited free customer support
questions.explain: GDPR grants data-subject rights including access, rectification, erasure (the 'right to be forgotten'), restriction, portability, and objection.
